ui.title: One kit. Every surface.
ui.body: Base components from @app/ui — themes, shells, and composites. Import per subpath, restyle through tokens, never hardcode colors.

brand.title: Brand
brand.description: Logo icon + name (+ optional subtitle). Same mark on the marketing header, app sidebar, admin sidebar, and auth screens.

navItem.title: NavItem
navItem.description: One nav entry with header and sidebar variants. Active state comes from the router; icons are passed as nodes.

siteHeader.title: SiteHeader
siteHeader.description: Sticky public header chrome: brand, nav row, and trailing actions (theme toggles, CTAs).

sidebar.title: Sidebar
sidebar.description: App chrome slots — header (brand), nav (items), footer (toggles + user menu). Pass the composed tree into SidebarShell.

sidebarShell.title: SidebarShell
sidebarShell.description: App chrome with a lateral menu + main. Pass a composed Sidebar; set resizable for the drag handle (app) or omit it for a fixed width (admin).

navbarShell.title: NavbarShell
navbarShell.description: Public chrome with a top navbar + scrolling main + optional footer. Marketing and docs pages.

authShell.title: AuthShell
authShell.description: Centered auth chrome: brand above a card (title / description / body) and an optional footer. Login, register, recovery.

userMenu.title: UserMenuButton
userMenu.description: Avatar + name + email trigger. Dropdown content stays in the app layer.

iconButton.title: Icon button
iconButton.description: Button size="icon" — the same control ThemeControls uses for language, palette, and mode.

button.title: Button
button.description: Primary actions with variants for hierarchy and sizes for density.

badge.title: Badge
badge.description: Compact labels for status, counts, and metadata.

progress.title: Progress
progress.description: Pill progress bar. Use alone or with showValue for bar + percent — compose labels and actions outside.

slider.title: Slider
slider.description: Accessible range slider. Controlled with value={[n]}; compose title, badge, and helper text around it.

label.title: Label
label.description: Accessible field label. Pair with htmlFor matching the control id.

input.title: Input
input.description: Single-line text field. Shared border, height, and focus ring with the rest of the form kit.

textarea.title: Textarea
textarea.description: Multi-line text field. Same tokens as Input — taller by default.

combobox.title: Combobox
combobox.description: Searchable select with icons and optional groups. Same chrome as Input — drop-in for native <select>.

field.title: Field
field.description: Label + control layout. vertical stacks above the control; horizontal is a min-h-9 row that lines up with Input in grids.

checkbox.title: Checkbox
checkbox.description: Boolean choice. Use Field orientation="horizontal" so it aligns with Input height.

radioGroup.title: RadioGroup
radioGroup.description: Single choice from a set. orientation vertical (default) or horizontal for an inline row.

switch.title: Switch
switch.description: On/off toggle. Same Field horizontal pairing as Checkbox — bottoms align next to Input.

form.title: Form
form.description: All form controls stacked with Field — vertical fields, horizontal checks/toggles, and a grid row with Input + Switch.

card.title: Card
card.description: Surface for grouped content — header, body, and footer slots.

avatar.title: Avatar
avatar.description: User initials (or image) in a circular fallback.

dialog.title: Dialog
dialog.description: Modal overlay for focused tasks. Close label is passed in for i18n.

dropdown.title: Dropdown menu
dropdown.description: Contextual actions anchored to a trigger.

page.title: PageHeader, EmptyState & PageLoading
page.description: The three building blocks every internal list page uses.

dataTable.title: DataTable
dataTable.description: Column-driven table with client-side sort (click any header that has sortValue) and optional pagination. Pass labels from the app for i18n; omit pageSize to render every row.

tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.description: Composable tabs for pages, cards, or dialogs — list, triggers, and content panels. Controlled or uncontrolled via value / defaultValue.

barChart.title: BarChart
barChart.description: Simple bar chart over Recharts. Pass rows, an index key, and one or more series keys — colors come from theme tokens (--chart-1…5).

lineChart.title: LineChart
lineChart.description: Same data shape as BarChart. Optional curve and dots; legend appears automatically with multiple series.

pieChart.title: PieChart
pieChart.description: Pie or donut from { name, value } rows. Set innerRadius for a donut; legend and tooltip are on by default.

structureEnvironment.title: Docker. Env. Run. Ship.
structureEnvironment.body: Local Postgres in Compose, one validated .env, two commands to click the app, then render.yaml for production — same knobs from laptop to Render.

local.title: Docker → env → run
local.body: Boot Postgres in Docker, fill .env (validated at boot), then setup + dev. No local Postgres install.

ship.title: One YAML on Render
ship.body: render.yaml describes the web service and managed Postgres. Secrets stay in the dashboard. No custom Dockerfile — Node runtime.

overview.title: The files that define the environment
overview.body: Compose for local Postgres, .env.example as the contract, render.yaml for production, env.ts to validate at boot. Closed here — opened next.
overview.aria: Environment-related files in a VS Code-style explorer

docker.title: Postgres in Compose
docker.body: The only Docker dependency is local Postgres. docker-compose.yml runs postgres:16 on :5442 with a named volume. Production uses managed Postgres on Render — not this container.

env.title: One file, local defaults
env.body: Copy .env.example to .env. DATABASE_URL and APP_URL have working local defaults. Optional keys degrade gracefully — no Resend? emails print to the console; no OpenAI? the agent hides.
points: optional keys never crash the boot
same names as Render env vars

envSchema.title: Validated at boot
envSchema.body: Zod parses process.env when the API starts. Missing or malformed required shape fails fast with a clear message. Defaults cover local; production injects values from Render.

run.title: setup, then dev
run.body: npm run setup brings Postgres up, migrates, and seeds a demo workspace. npm run dev starts the API and SPA together — click a real app in under a minute.

renderYaml.title: The production blueprint
renderYaml.body: One web service (API serves the built SPA) plus managed Postgres 16. build, start, preDeploy migrate, health check, auto-deploy on push to main — described once in YAML.

renderConnect.title: Connect the GitHub repo
renderConnect.body: In Render: New Blueprint → pick the repository that contains render.yaml → Connect. Render reads the file, provisions the web service and Postgres, and wires auto-deploy from that repo.
points: Connect on the repo with render.yaml

renderDeploy.title: Push to main, go live
renderDeploy.body: Render builds on push, runs migrations before traffic shifts, and only goes live after /api/health passes. The dashboard lists the web service and the Postgres instance from the blueprint.

renderEnv.title: Where production values are set
renderEnv.body: Open the web service → Environment. Keys match .env / render.yaml; values stay masked in the dashboard. Edit there for anything marked sync: false — never put real secrets in git.

secrets.title: sync: false — out of git
secrets.body: Secret values never live in the repo. .env is gitignored; .env.example only has placeholders. On Render, sync: false means the value is set in the dashboard. DATABASE_URL comes from the managed database link.

runtime.title: No app Dockerfile
runtime.body: Production is Render's native Node runtime — not a custom Docker image. Docker in this repo is only for local Postgres via Compose. Desktop/mobile installers build in GitHub Actions, not on Render.
runtime.visualNoDocker: ls: Dockerfile: No such file or directory

structureStorage.title: MediaStore. Disk. R2.
structureStorage.body: One put/get interface for files. Local disk while you build; Cloudflare R2 when Render's filesystem would throw the bytes away.

r2.title: Bucket, public URL, credentials
r2.body: Create a bucket, turn on public access, mint an R2 token, then paste CLOUDFLARE_* and R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL into Render. Domains keep calling mediaStore — only the backend changes.

overview.title: Where file storage lives
overview.body: lib/media-store.ts is the contract. integrations/r2.ts talks S3 to Cloudflare. article/utils picks the backend at boot and compresses uploads. Closed here — opened next.
overview.aria: Storage-related API files in a VS Code-style explorer

contract.title: One interface for every file
contract.body: Domains never import the S3 SDK. They call put, get, has, remove on MediaStore. Keys stay tenant-scoped — the same relative path shape whether bytes land on disk or in R2.

backends.title: R2 when configured, disk otherwise
backends.body: isR2Configured() checks endpoint, keys, and public URL. Missing any piece → localStore under MEDIA_DIR. That keeps local setup zero-config and production durable.
points: DB stores the same relative path

write.title: Compress, then put
write.body: Uploads go through sharp → WebP before mediaStore.put. Callers get back a public path and compressed size — never raw upload bytes on disk or in the bucket.
points: path stored on the article row

local.title: Fine for dev, wrong for Render
local.body: Without R2 credentials, files land under MEDIA_DIR (often apps/web/public). That works on your laptop. Render's disk is ephemeral — set R2 before you care about covers surviving a deploy.

r2Buckets.title: Create the app bucket
r2Buckets.body: In Cloudflare: R2 Object Storage → Create bucket. Name it to match CLOUDFLARE_MEDIA_BUCKET (default app). Note the Account ID — it appears in the S3 endpoint.

r2Objects.title: Empty is fine — public access on
r2Objects.body: The bucket starts empty; the API writes objects via S3. Enable public access so browsers can load covers from the public URL without the API proxying bytes.
points: API writes via S3, not drag-drop
app.ts redirects to the public URL

r2Settings.title: S3 API + public development URL
r2Settings.body: Copy the S3 API host into CLOUDFLARE_S3_API (account endpoint, no secrets). Copy the public development URL (or a custom domain) into R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Without that origin, isR2Configured stays false.
points: public URL required to enable R2

r2Tokens.title: Credentials for the S3 client
r2Tokens.body: Create an account token with R2 Storage edit. Cloudflare shows an Access Key ID and Secret Access Key once — those become CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS_KEY_ID and CLOUDFLARE_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY on Render (sync: false).

r2CreateToken.title: Workers R2 Storage · Edit
r2CreateToken.body: Filter permissions by r2, grant Workers R2 Storage Edit on the account, create the token, then copy the S3 credentials into env. Read-only is not enough for cover uploads.

r2Env.title: R2 keys on Render
r2Env.body: Paste CLOUDFLARE_* and R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL in the Render Environment dashboard. Secrets use sync: false. Partial config counts as off — local disk until every piece is set.
r2Env.visualFootnote: sync: false on secrets; without the public URL, R2 stays off.

r2Integration.title: S3 against Cloudflare
r2Integration.body: The R2 backend is a thin MediaStore over @aws-sdk/client-s3. region auto, endpoint from env. Domains stay on mediaStore — only this file knows about PutObjectCommand.

structureOpenai.title: Key. Loop. Agent.
structureOpenai.body: One optional secret powers the assistant. Without it the FAB hides and the rest of the app keeps working. With it, integrations/openai runs the tool loop and agent/assistant owns the product policy.

keys.title: Mint the secret, paste once
keys.body: Create a secret key in the OpenAI dashboard, set OPENAI_API_KEY on Render (sync: false), and the in-app agent lights up. Never commit the sk- value.

overview.title: Where the AI stack lives
overview.body: integrations/openai.ts owns the SDK and the tool-calling loop. agent/assistant.ts is product policy. Domain tools never import openai — lint enforces it. Closed here — opened next.
overview.aria: OpenAI and agent files in a VS Code-style explorer

hasKey.title: Optional — degrade gracefully
hasKey.body: No key means the agent stays hidden and chat returns 503. Everything else — auth, tenants, tasks — keeps working. Same pattern as Resend and R2.
points: no vendor account required to develop

loop.title: Model → tools → model
loop.body: The only file that imports the openai package. It runs chat completions with tools, executes each call, feeds results back, and returns usage for the billing ledger.
points: tool results go back to the model
swap provider here without touching domains

assistant.title: Policy, not the SDK
assistant.body: runAssistant maps registry tools onto the loop, builds the system prompt from tenant context, and streams status chips. Tenant and user always come from ctx — never from the model inventing ids.

keys.title: Your keys on platform.openai.com
keys.body: Open API keys, create a secret for this product, keep it Active. The dashboard shows a masked sk-… — the full value appears only at creation.
points: API keys in the left nav
track spend per key if you want

createKey.title: Name it, then copy once
createKey.body: Create new secret key → name it after your product → Permissions All (or restrict later) → Create. Paste into OPENAI_API_KEY immediately; you will not see the full string again.

env.title: OPENAI_API_KEY on Render
env.body: Open the web service → Environment → Edit. Paste the secret once with sync: false. ASSISTANT_MODEL is optional. Empty key → agent off; the rest of the app keeps working.
env.visualFootnote: sync: false — paste OPENAI_API_KEY via Environment → Edit.

chat.title: What the key unlocks
chat.body: With the key set, the floating assistant can list and mutate tenant resources through tools. Product UI for the agent lives under /product/agent — this page is the credential and integration path.
points: FAB only when the key exists

structureResend.title: Key. Domain. Inbox.
structureResend.body: Transactional email through one sendEmail helper. Without RESEND_API_KEY, messages log to the console. With a verified domain and a key, verify / reset / invite land in real inboxes.

dashboard.title: API key + verified domain
dashboard.body: Create a sending key, add DNS for your domain, then set RESEND_API_KEY and MAIL_FROM on Render. MAIL_FROM must use a domain Resend has verified.

overview.title: Where email lives
overview.body: integrations/resend.ts owns the HTTP call. lib/email.ts builds the HTML shell. Auth, tenant, and admin call sendEmail — they never import Resend. Closed here — opened next.
overview.aria: Resend and email files in a VS Code-style explorer

send.title: Send or log — never block
send.body: No key → log subject and size (never HTML — tokens live in links). With a key → POST to api.resend.com using MAIL_FROM. Fire-and-forget so the HTTP response stays fast.

layout.title: One HTML shell for every CTA mail
layout.body: Verify, reset password, tenant invite, platform invite — same layout helper, different title/body/CTA. Keep tokens out of logs; they only appear inside the emailed link.

keys.title: Create a sending key
keys.body: In Resend: API keys → Create. Prefer Sending access for production. The re_… token is shown once — that value is RESEND_API_KEY.

createKey.title: Name, permission, domain scope
createKey.body: Name the key after your product, pick Full or Sending access, scope to All domains or one verified domain, then Add. Paste into Render immediately.

domains.title: Add the domain you send from
domains.body: MAIL_FROM must use a verified domain. Add domain in Resend, publish the DNS records they give you, wait until Status is Verified.

domainDetail.title: Ready to send
domainDetail.body: When DNS verifies, Resend marks the domain ready. From there MAIL_FROM like App Base <hello@mail.example.com> will deliver instead of bouncing.

env.title: RESEND_API_KEY on Render
env.body: Same Environment tab as other secrets. Set RESEND_API_KEY (sync: false) and MAIL_FROM to an address on a verified domain. No key → emails log to the console.
env.visualFootnote: sync: false on the key; MAIL_FROM uses a verified domain.

inbox.title: Invites and auth mail
inbox.body: Same sendEmail path powers verify, reset, and invites. Product pages walk those flows; this page is the Resend credential and domain setup.

structureBuild.title: Everything above is the template. Now build yours.
structureBuild.body: What you just walked is the model {{brand}} ships ready — packages, env, database, storage, i18n. Your product starts when you add your own resources: a schema, a repository, routes and tools. The API page shows that pattern end to end with tasks — copy the folder, rename it, register it, ship.
structureBuild.cta: See how to add a resource
structureBuild.hint: Schema → repository → tools → DTOs → routes — then mirror it on the web.

closing.skipDemo: Or skip the demo — clone the repo and start building.

footer.builtWith: Built with React, Hono and Postgres

theming.title: Kit themes, brand when you need it
theming.bodyBefore: Light and dark palettes ship with @app/ui. The primary color drives buttons, highlights and focus rings; the rest is neutral surfaces. ThemeProvider writes CSS variables onto the page — the whole UI recolors with no component edits, no
theming.bodyAfter: classes to chase. Extend with createTheme when your product needs its own accent.
theming.tryIt: Try it — this page changes as you click. Your choice is saved and shared with the app.

i18n.title: Two JSON files, one t() call
i18n.body: UI copy lives in locale files — English is the source of truth, Portuguese ships beside it. Components never hardcode strings: they call t("…"), and the language picker (or the browser) does the rest. Add a key to both files and every screen that uses it updates.
points: en.json + pt.json under apps/web/src/i18n/locales/ — same keys, two languages
useTranslation() and t("tasks.title") — no providers to wire per page
Preference sticks in localStorage; first visit follows the browser language
This landing page is translated the same way as the app shell
i18n.tryIt: Try it — switch language here and the whole page follows, including this section.

database.title: Postgres first. Then the ORM.
database.body: The engine is Postgres. Drizzle models tables, runs queries, and generates migrations. Walk the stack, then the tables that ship, then the demo seed.

queries.title: Schema done — now use it
queries.body: Everything below lives in the domain repository. Imports, reads, writes, operators — one idea per section.

migrations.title: Schema → SQL → database
migrations.body: Never hand-write migration SQL. Generate from the TypeScript schema, commit the files, apply pending ones — locally and on every deploy.

schema.title: Tables by domain
schema.body: Each domain owns its schema/. Identity, tenancy, plans, usage, articles, the example resource, platform invites.

seed.title: Seed so you can click
seed.body: After migrate, seed puts a demo user, workspace, and sample tasks in place — idempotent, safe to re-run.

postgres.title: The engine
postgres.body: Postgres 16 is the only database. Locally it runs in Docker; in production it is managed Postgres on Render.

drizzle.title: Declare the table
drizzle.body: First you model the table: pgTable, columns, FK, index. That file is the source of truth — generate migrations from it, then query it from the repository.

queryImports.title: Where things come from
queryImports.body: Three sources in every repository: operators from drizzle-orm, the live db from @/db/client, and your pgTable from ./schema. Column helpers for new tables come from drizzle-orm/pg-core.

querySelect.title: select · from · where
querySelect.body: Reads chain left to right like SQL: what you want, which table, optional join, filters, sort. tenantId belongs in every where for tenant-scoped data.

queryWrites.title: insert · update · delete
queryWrites.body: Mutations end with .returning() so you get the row back. Drizzle returns an array — destructure [row]. Updates and deletes filter by id and tenantId together.

queryOperators.title: The everyday toolbox
queryOperators.body: eq, and, or, ilike, desc, asc — the filters and sorts you reach for constantly. Missing tenantId in a where is a cross-tenant leak.

migrateFlow.title: The two commands
migrateFlow.body: Edit a pgTable, export it from db/schema.ts, then generate. drizzle-kit diffs the schema against the last snapshot and writes numbered SQL. migrate applies whatever is still pending on DATABASE_URL.

migrateFiles.title: Where they are saved
migrateFiles.body: Generated SQL and meta snapshots live under apps/api/drizzle/. Commit that folder — teammates and Render replay the same history. drizzle.config.ts points schema at the barrel and out at this directory.
migrateFiles.aria: drizzle migrations folder in a VS Code-style explorer

migrateExample.title: What generate writes
migrateExample.body: You change the TypeScript schema — say you add a publishedAt column. db:generate diffs that against the last snapshot and emits a numbered SQL file: ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN, maybe an index. Same shape for every real migration in apps/api/drizzle/.
points: ADD COLUMN · CREATE INDEX · ADD CONSTRAINT…
commit the file · migrate applies it

migrateWhen.title: Local setup and every deploy
migrateWhen.body: Locally, npm run setup migrates after Postgres is up. Anytime after that, db:migrate catches pending files. In production, render.yaml runs migrate as preDeployCommand — before traffic hits the new build.

seed.title: Demo user, tenant, tasks
seed.body: Idempotent seed for local (and setup). Creates a platform-admin demo user, a Demo Company workspace, and a few tasks so the SPA is not empty.
points: sample tasks — replace with your domain

resourceIntro.title: One resource, top to bottom
resourceIntro.bodyAfter: is the placeholder domain. Same name on API and web, fixed roles on each side, one shared contract in packages/shared. Walk the API (table → schema/<table>.schema.ts → repository → route → tool), then the React domain (folder → api.ts → routes → page), and land on the screen. Copy that folder pair for your own resource.

structureLinks.title: Pick a package to open
structureLinks.body: Each deep-dive walks that package’s folders and conventions — same guided style as the monorepo overview above.
structureLinks.platformBody: Env, database, object storage, OpenAI, Resend, custom domain, and i18n — the pieces every feature leans on.

api.title: Backend API
api.body: Domains, schema, repository, endpoints, DTOs, tools — one folder each.

web.title: The React SPA
web.body: Domains that mirror the API — api.ts, pages, routes, and shell chrome.

ui.title: The UI kit
ui.body: Primitives, shell, composites, and theme — the app-neutral building blocks.

environment.title: Docker → env → Render
environment.body: Compose for local Postgres, validated .env, setup/dev, then one YAML on Render.

database.title: Postgres → Drizzle → tables
database.body: Engine, ORM, shipped schemas by domain, and the demo seed.

storage.title: Files via MediaStore
storage.body: One interface for uploads — Cloudflare R2 in production, local disk when you skip credentials.

openai.title: API key → agent loop
openai.body: Optional secret, tool-calling integration, and graceful hide when the key is missing.

resend.title: API key → real email
resend.body: Optional secret, verified domain, and console fallback when the key is missing.

i18n.title: English and Portuguese
i18n.body: Locale JSON files and t() — switch language live and the whole UI follows.

domain.title: CNAME → Render
domain.body: Add a custom host on Render, point a CNAME at your registrar, set APP_URL when the certificate is issued.

monorepo.title: One repo. Workspaces, Turbo, one deploy.
monorepo.body: Everything lives in one npm workspaces + Turborepo repo: the Hono API, the React SPA, shared Zod contracts, and the UI kit. Turbo wires the task graph; render.yaml ships API + SPA as one service with managed Postgres.
points: apps/api, apps/web, packages/shared, packages/ui — one graph, not four repos
turbo.json defines the build/lint/typecheck pipeline across packages
render.yaml: one web service (API serves the SPA) + managed Postgres
packages/shared is the typed contract — change a shape, the forgotten side fails to compile

api.title: Backend API
api.body: Map first. Then each folder — role, boundary, keywords.

layout.title: One folder per domain
layout.body: domains/ = features. lib/ = infra. agent/ · integrations/ = shared surfaces. Closed here — opened next.

web.title: Frontend SPA
web.body: Map first. Then each folder — role, boundary, keywords.

layout.title: Same domain names as the API
layout.body: domains/ = features. app/ · layouts/ = shell. lib/ · i18n/ · theme/ · brand/ = shared chrome. Closed here — opened next.

ui.title: The UI kit
ui.body: App-neutral building blocks, grouped by role. Import per subpath — restyle through theme tokens, never hardcode colors.
points: composites/ + theme/ — higher patterns and palettes
ui.aria: packages/ui folder tree in a VS Code-style explorer

domain.title: Fixed roles
domain.body: schema → repository → DTO → endpoints → tools. Optional: service · middleware · constants · utils · template.

domains.title: Features
domains.body: One folder = one feature. Same name on the frontend.
points: resource — schema · repository · DTO · endpoints · tools

lib.title: Infra
lib.body: Shared primitives. No domain knowledge. Nothing imports back into lib/.

integrations.title: Vendors
integrations.body: External services. Thin wrappers. Only talk to lib/.

db.title: Database
db.body: Client, shared columns, schema barrel, seed. Tables live in domains.

agent.title: Assistant surface
agent.body: Chat + remote tools. Domains register tools; they don't own this folder.

app.title: Mounts
app.body: Wire every route group once. Server listens. Context = request types.
points: public · invite · join · remote tools — second mounts
auth + tenant guards on the group

schema.title: Tables
schema.body: One table per file. Tenant-scoped. Index + type export.

repository.title: SQL boundary
repository.body: All queries here. Every method takes tenantId. Returns rows — not DTOs.
points: routes / tools call this — no SQL elsewhere

dto.title: Wire shape
dto.body: Map row → DTO. Explicit fields. Never spread a row.

routes.title: Endpoints
routes.body: One file per endpoint. Group map in index. Guards once on the group.
points: tenant / user from context — never from body

tools.title: Agent actions
tools.body: One file per action. Same repository as endpoints. Registered in the assistant.

service.title: Business rules
service.body: Orchestration only. Plain CRUD skips this file.

middleware.title: Guards
middleware.body: Auth · tenant · role. Applied once on the route group.

utils.title: Helpers
utils.body: Domain logic helpers. lib/ stays cross-cutting and pure.

template.title: Outbound mail
template.body: Subject + body. Service sends. Token only in the link.

domain.title: Fixed roles
domain.body: api.ts → pages → routes → components. Optional: context · hooks · constants · utils.

domains.title: Features
domains.body: One folder = one feature. Same name as the API.

app.title: Route map
app.body: Compose top-level groups once. Server-driven flags live here.

layouts.title: Shells
layouts.body: App chrome and auth gate. Domains don't own layout.

lib.title: Infra
lib.body: Raw HTTP and pure helpers. No domain knowledge.
points: domains wrap this — pages never call it raw

i18n.title: Copy
i18n.body: Every user-facing string. Never hardcode in JSX.
points: add keys to both files of the pair

theme.title: Controls
theme.body: Language · palette · mode. Tokens live in @app/ui.

brand.title: Mark
brand.body: Product logo only. Display name lives in shared.

api.title: Network boundary
api.body: Typed calls for this domain. The only place that hits the network.
points: pages never fetch or call lib/api raw

pages.title: Screens
pages.body: One route screen per file. Query for reads, mutation for writes.
points: tenant from useTenant — never parse the URL

routes.title: Route element
routes.body: Domain owns its <Route>. Tenant composes under :tenantSlug.
points: every domain with pages exports one

components.title: Domain UI
components.body: Product UI for this feature. kebab-case. No top-level dump.
points: create with the first non-page piece

context.title: Provider
context.body: Shared React state for the domain. Provider + useX together.
points: add folder with the first provider

hooks.title: React helpers
hooks.body: Reusable hooks that aren't the context consumer.

constants.title: Statics
constants.body: Keys · catalogs · limits. Same role as the API. Optional.

config.title: One .env, validated at boot
config.body: Everything the app reads comes from a single .env, checked by Zod when the process starts — a missing or malformed var fails fast with a clear message. Only two things matter to run locally, and they already have working defaults; the rest are optional and degrade gracefully.
points: DATABASE_URL and APP_URL are all you need — both default for local dev
No RESEND_API_KEY? Emails print to the console instead of sending
No OPENAI_API_KEY? The AI agent is simply hidden — nothing breaks
SELF_SIGNUP_ENABLED flips the app between open signup and invite-only
PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS lists emails that are always platform admins once verified

storage.title: Object storage, ready before you need it
storage.body: Any domain that has to store a file — images, avatars, exports, whatever your product needs — goes through one small interface: put, get, has, remove. Add R2 credentials and it writes straight to Cloudflare's object storage with a public URL; leave them out and it falls back to the local disk, so there's a resource to build on from day one, not a feature you have to wire yourself.
points: MediaStore is the only interface a domain touches — swap the backend without touching callers
No R2 credentials? Falls back to the local disk automatically — nothing to configure to start
Images already run through it, compressed to WebP on write — copy that domain for your own files

localRun.title: One command, the whole stack up
localRun.body: No local Postgres to install: npm run setup uses Docker to boot Postgres 16, applies the migrations and seeds a demo workspace. npm run dev then starts the API and the SPA together — you're clicking a real app in under a minute.
points: Docker Compose runs Postgres on :5442 — nothing to install by hand
setup migrates and seeds a demo tenant and user for you
npm run dev boots the API (:5000) and the SPA (:3000) at once
The .env ships with working local defaults, validated at boot

render.title: Deploys to Render from one YAML
render.body: Production is described once in render.yaml: a single web service that runs the API and serves the built SPA, plus a managed Postgres. Push to main and Render builds, runs migrations on pre-deploy, and health-checks before going live — no deploy scripts to write.
points: One web service (API + SPA, one origin) and one managed Postgres
Migrations run automatically on pre-deploy, before traffic shifts
Auto-deploy on push to main, gated by a /api/health check
Secrets stay out of the repo with sync: false

delete.title: Delete the example
delete.description: Tasks are a placeholder. Remove the domain, drop the table, and put your product's resources in its place — nothing else breaks.

unsubscribe.title: Nothing to unsubscribe from
unsubscribe.description: Auth is scrypt and cookies, email is one swappable module, deploy is a YAML file. Swap any piece without asking permission.

rules.title: Rewrite the rules
rules.description: The conventions are markdown in .cursor/rules/, each scoped by glob to the files it governs — so the agent reads the same playbook. Disagree with one? Edit it, and it follows you instead.

convention.title: A feature is a folder on both sides
convention.body: Domain-driven development here is literal: one feature = one folder named the same on the API and on the web, each with fixed roles — not a grab-bag of files. The API owns schema, repository, dto, routes and tools; the web owns api.ts, pages, routes.tsx and components (plus context/hooks when it needs shared React state). Both import the same Zod schema and DTO from packages/shared, so a shape change breaks the side you forgot to update.
points: Same domain name on apps/api and apps/web — never scatter a feature
API roles: schema → repository → dto → routes → tools
Web roles: api.ts → pages/ → routes.tsx → components/ (context/hooks; optional constants/utils like the API)
packages/shared is the contract both sides compile against
Boundaries fail the lint, not just code review

schema.title: A table is a pgTable in its domain
schema.body: The tasks table shows the exact shape every table you add will follow: a uuid primary key, a tenant_id foreign key that scopes it to a workspace, the timestamps helper, and an index on the tenant. Run db:generate and the SQL migration is derived from this file — the schema stays the source of truth.
points: tenant_id ties every row to a workspace and cascades on delete
author_id references the user but is nullable — set null on delete
Migrations are generated from the schema, never hand-written

schemaFile.title: The pgTable that creates it
schemaFile.body: That table is declared in schema/tasks.schema.ts with Drizzle's pgTable — one table per file: id, tenant FK with cascade, optional author, fields, …timestamps, and an index on tenantId. Export the inferred Task type from the same file and re-export from schema/index.ts. Register the domain in db/schema.ts, then db:generate writes the migration.
points: Copy domains/task/schema/tasks.schema.ts for every new tenant-scoped table
Export the domain from db/schema.ts, then npm run db:generate — never hand-write SQL

repositoryMethod.title: One method, one Drizzle query
repositoryMethod.body: Start here. A repository method is where the ORM runs — select, join, where, orderBy in plain TypeScript. list always filters by tenantId (isolation is not optional), optionally searches the title, joins the author, and returns rows. No hidden helpers; the whole query sits in the method.
points: Drizzle in the method body — this is the only place SQL lives
tenantId in every where — a missing filter is a cross-tenant leak
Returns DB rows / joins — not API DTOs yet

repository.title: Those methods live in one object
repository.body: Zoom out from list. find, insert, update, and delete sit beside it on a single exported taskRepository — fixed CRUD names, every method takes tenantId. Routes and tools call this object; they never write SQL. Mapping to the wire shape is the next step (dto.ts).
points: One object per resource: list / find / insert / update / delete
Same tenantId rule on every method you just saw in list
Callers stay thin — repository owns persistence

dto.title: Map rows explicitly — never spread a DB row
dto.body: dto.ts turns repository shapes into the shared TaskDto from packages/shared. Dates become ISO strings; password hashes and token hashes never leave the server. Routes and tools call toTaskDto — they don't invent response shapes inline.
points: Explicit field map in toXxxDto — never …row into JSON
Shared TaskDto lives in packages/shared — both sides compile against it
Dates are strings on the wire; secrets stay off the DTO

route.title: One handler, one HTTP route
route.body: Start here. A route file is named for the path and method relative to the mount — task.post.route.ts for POST /, tasks.get.route.ts for the list, task.get.route.ts for /:taskId. The handler stays a thin action (createTask): Input → Processing → Output. It validates with the shared schema, reads tenant and user from middleware context, calls the repository, and maps through the DTO. It never checks a session or resolves a tenant itself — that already ran on the group.
points: File name = path.method.route.ts (list plural, create/member singular)
Tenant from context, never from the request body
parseBody + repository + toXxxDto — no SQL in the route

routeMap.title: Those handlers live on one group
routeMap.body: Zoom out from createTask. list, get, update, delete hang beside it in routes/index.ts — requireAuth and requireTenant once via .use, then one line per handler. Same aggregator pattern as the repository object and the tool array. Mount the group in app.ts under /api/tenants/:tenantId/tasks.
points: Middleware once via .use — every route inherits auth + tenant
One line per handler: .get("/", listTasks), .post("/", createTask)
Add path.method.route.ts, import it here, done

tool.title: One defineTool, one action
tool.body: Start here. A tool file is how the agent learns a single action — name, description, Zod input, and execute that calls the repository you already wrote. create_task reuses taskRepository.insert; tenant and user come from ctx, never from the model guessing IDs. The same definition powers in-app chat and remote MCP.
points: defineTool in one file — no MCP or OpenAI imports (lint blocks them)
execute reuses the repository — tools don't invent a second data path
summarize marks a write — it shows up as a chip in the chat

toolMap.title: Those tools live in one array
toolMap.body: Zoom out from create_task. list, get, update, delete sit beside it in tools/index.ts as taskTools — same role as the repository object for SQL. Spread that array into agent/registry.ts allTools and every surface picks it up. Add a tool file, push it onto the array, done.
points: One array per domain: export const taskTools: AgentTool[] = […]
Mirrors routes/index.ts — folder owns its index

webConvention.title: Same name, different roles
webConvention.body: After the API half, the web domain for the same feature. api.ts is the network boundary; pages/ are route screens; routes.tsx exports the domain's <Route>; components/ holds product UI for that domain only. context/ and hooks/ appear when the domain needs shared React state — auth and tenant already do. Optional constants/ and utils/ match the API (static values vs non-React helpers); React helpers stay in hooks/. Base UI (Button, PageHeader, EmptyState, useConfirm…) comes from @app/ui; there is no top-level src/components/ dump.
points: domains/<feature>/ — api.ts, pages/, routes.tsx; components/ with the first UI piece
context/<name>-provider.tsx co-locates Provider + useX; hooks/ for React; optional constants/utils like the API
Product UI stays in the owning domain — never a shared components dump
@app/ui is tenant-agnostic; app/, layouts/, theme/, i18n/, lib/ are shell

api.title: One api.ts wraps every call
api.body: The only file that touches the network is the domain's api.ts — a thin object over the shared HTTP client, returning the same DTO the API sends. Pages never call fetch or the raw client directly, so every request for a resource has exactly one place to change. The tenant id is part of the path, mirroring /api/tenants/:tenantId/… on the server.
points: Network only through the domain api.ts — never a raw fetch in a page
Returns the shared DTO type — typed end to end with packages/shared

webRoutes.title: Own your Route in one file
webRoutes.body: Each domain exports its <Route> from routes.tsx — one line for tasks, same pattern for articles, billing, account. The domain decides the path and the page; it doesn't know about the shell.
points: Same file role on every feature domain
No auth checks here — the shell already wrapped the tree

webRouteMap.title: Compose under the tenant
webRouteMap.body: tenant/routes.tsx mounts every domain under :tenantSlug and AppLayout. Drop a new domain's routes into that composition, add a nav item, done. RequireAuth and TenantProvider sit on the shell — pages don't re-check the session.
points: Adding a feature = export routes + compose + nav link
RequireAuth and TenantProvider wrap the shell, not each page

page.title: Queries + chrome from @app/ui
page.body: Every internal page starts the same way: useTenant() for the workspace (TenantProvider — the React parallel to API middleware), useQuery keyed by the tenant for reads, then PageHeader / PageLoading / EmptyState so the page stays about the feature.
points: useTenant() — tenant from context, never parsed ad hoc in the page
useQuery keyed by tenant.id for every list/detail read
PageHeader, PageLoading, EmptyState from @app/ui — same chrome every page

pageWrites.title: Mutations invalidate; deletes confirm
pageWrites.body: Writes are useMutation with invalidateQueries on success — no manual loading flags. Destructive actions go through useConfirm; failures surface with showApiError(). Same shape for create, update, and delete.
points: useMutation + invalidateQueries on success — no local loading state
useConfirm() for destructive actions, never window.confirm
showApiError(err, fallback) for every mutation onError

screen.title: The result: a full CRUD feature
screen.body: That's the whole slice — API and web — and this is the screen it powers. Per-tenant create, list, toggle and delete, wired end to end through the shared DTO. Copy both domain folders, rename them, register the routes and tools, and your resource lands exactly here.
points: Per-tenant create, list, toggle and delete out of the box
The exact shape you'll clone for your product's resources
Delete the example and drop yours in — nothing else breaks

signIn.title: Login, clean and familiar
signIn.body: Email, password, a link to recovery, and secure sessions on submit — scrypt hashing and an httpOnly cookie, no auth vendor. Built with shadcn/ui, ready to rebrand.

signUp.title: Registration that sets everything up
signUp.body: Name, email, password. Each new user gets a personal tenant automatically — no empty account sitting around waiting for a workspace.

verifyEmail.title: A link lands in the inbox
verifyEmail.body: Sign-up sends a verification email with a single-use link that expires in 24 hours. Until they click it, the account stays unverified.

forgotPassword.title: Ask for a reset link
forgotPassword.body: Enter the email on /forgot-password. The server mints a short-lived token and sends the reset mail — same pattern as verification, different purpose.

resetEmail.title: The inbox carries the token
resetEmail.body: The message holds a one-time link. The raw token never hits the database — only its hash — so a leaked dump can't forge a reset.

resetPassword.title: Set it on a guarded screen
resetPassword.body: /reset-password validates the token server-side, then hashes the new password with scrypt and ends every other session for that user.

shell.title: A workspace, not a blank page
shell.body: Sidebar nav, a tenant switcher that appears only with more than one, a user menu and the theme controls. Your screens drop straight into the outlet.

agent.title: A chat that gets things done
agent.body: A floating assistant in every tenant: ask or command, it runs the right tools, shows what changed as a chip, and refreshes the data on its own.

account.title: Profile, security, and where keys live
account.body: Every user manages their own profile and password from My account. API keys for the remote MCP server live under Integrations — same patterns you'll reuse for any personal settings you add.

inviteMembers.title: Pick an email and a role
inviteMembers.body: Owners and admins invite from settings — members and pending invites in one place, each revocable. Seat caps from the tenant plan block invites when the workspace is full.

inviteEmail.title: A 7-day link in their inbox
inviteEmail.body: The invite lands as transactional email with a single-use link. Accepting it joins the workspace under the role you chose.

adminPeople.title: Every account on the platform
adminPeople.body: Platform admins see every user across tenants — orthogonal to workspace roles. Bootstrap access with PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS.

adminInvites.title: Invite people to the product
adminInvites.body: Send a platform invite so someone can sign up for their own workspace — not join yours. Different from tenant member invites.

adminInviteEmail.title: The platform invite lands here
adminInviteEmail.body: Same email machinery as tenant invites — a link, an expiry, a hash in the database — aimed at creating a new account and workspace.

plansCatalog.title: Seats and AI entitlements in code
plansCatalog.body: Four plans — Free, Starter, Pro, and Pay as you go — with seat caps and per-member AI allowances. The catalog is data you own; wire Stripe when you're ready.

plansAssign.title: Platform admin sets the tenant plan
plansAssign.body: Pick a workspace and assign a planId. Tenants see usage under Billing; checkout later only needs to flip that field.

mcp.title: The same tools, over MCP
mcp.body: Mint a tenant-scoped API key under Integrations and plug the remote MCP server into Cursor or Claude — the agent's tools, right in your editor.

identity.title: Users, sessions and tokens
identity.body: The auth domain owns everything about a person: their credentials, the sessions that keep them signed in, and the single-use tokens emailed for verification and password resets. Passwords are scrypt hashes; sessions and tokens store only a hash, never the raw value.
points: users holds the account; a unique email is the login
sessions and action_tokens reference user_id and cascade on delete
api_keys are personal and scoped to one tenant for MCP access

tenancy.title: Workspaces and who belongs to them
tenancy.body: Every account works inside a tenant. tenant_members is the join table between users and tenants with a role, and tenant_invites carries pending invitations by email. plan_id on the tenant picks seats and AI limits from the code catalog — this is the backbone that makes the whole app multi-tenant.
points: tenant_members has a composite key of (tenant_id, user_id)
role is an enum — owner, admin, member — enforced at the type level
plan_id selects Free / Starter / Pro / usage entitlements (no Stripe required yet)
Invites expire and carry the role the person will get on accept

billing.title: Entitlements live in a code catalog
billing.body: There is no plans table. domains/billing/constants/plans.constants.ts exports PLAN_CATALOG — Free, Starter, Pro, and Pay as you go — with seat caps and per-member AI allowances. Lookups live in billing/utils. Tenants only store plan_id; platform admin assigns it. Wire Stripe later by writing the same field.
points: Four plans in code — edit the catalog when you fork
Seats + AI included vs passthrough, resolved by getPlan(planId)
Billing page reads the catalog + live usage — no payment provider yet

usage.title: An append-only spend ledger
usage.body: ai_usage_events records one row per assistant request: model, tokens, rounds, and cost in micro-dollars (USD × 1_000_000 — integers only). Spend aggregates per (userId, tenantId) against the tenant plan. The usage domain is ledger-only; the Billing UI is the face of it.
points: cost_micros never uses floats — micros keep money as integers
Scoped by user + tenant so seats and AI limits stay honest
No HTTP routes here — billing service reads the repository

articles.title: Articles with Markdown and a cover
articles.body: The articles table stores title, Markdown body, and optional cover metadata for tenant-scoped posts. Cover bytes live in object storage (local disk in dev, R2 in production) — the row is provenance plus the text.
points: tenant_id cascade; author_id set null on user delete
cover_path is the storage key, e.g. <tenantId>/uploads/<uuid>.webp
Richer CRUD than tasks — list/detail, upload, and agent-generated covers

tasks.title: Tasks — the placeholder you replace
tasks.body: tasks is the template tenant-scoped table: id, tenant_id, optional author, fields, timestamps. Copy this shape for your product resource, then delete the domain when you are ready.
points: tenant_id cascade — every row belongs to a workspace
author_id set null on user delete
Same pattern every new resource follows

platform.title: Signup invites outside any tenant
platform.body: platform_invites belongs to the admin domain: email + hashed token + expiry, with no tenant_id. Accepting creates a personal workspace. Orthogonal to tenant_invites — those bring people into an existing workspace.
points: Invite-only mode when SELF_SIGNUP_ENABLED is false
Token stored hashed; single-use with a TTL

forgot.title: Forgot password
forgot.description: We'll email you a reset link.

reset.title: Choose a new password
reset.description: Set a new password for your account.

verifyEmail.subject: Confirm your email
verifyEmail.heading: Confirm your email
verifyEmail.body: Hi {{name}}! Confirm your email address to finish signing up. This link expires in 24 hours.

resetEmail.subject: Reset your password
resetEmail.heading: Reset your password
resetEmail.body: We got a request to reset your password. This link is single-use and expires in 1 hour. If it wasn't you, ignore this email.

platformInviteEmail.subject: You're invited to {{brand}}
platformInviteEmail.heading: You're invited to {{brand}}
platformInviteEmail.bodyBefore: {{name}} invited you to create an account and try the app. This invite expires in 7 days.

admin.subtitle: Platform administration
admin.invitesDescription: Invite people to create an account and try the app
admin.tenantsDescription: Every workspace — people, plan, and edit in one place

plans.title: Plans
plans.description: Catalog in code — seats and AI entitlements
plans.pspHint: Ready for Stripe or any PSP — checkout sets planId

invites.title: Invites
invites.description: Invite people to this tenant by email
invites.membersDescription: Who has access to this tenant

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.left: Example resource with per-tenant CRUD · 2 of 4 left

agent.title: Assistant
agent.suggestion: Add a task to prepare tomorrow's standup
agent.reply: Sure — I'll add that task for you.
agent.chipError: Task not found — check the id with list_tasks
agent.chipsUser: Create the standup task and mark yesterday done
agent.intro: Ask or request something about Acme. Examples:

platformsIntro.title: One UI. Five places it runs.
platformsIntro.body: apps/web is the product. Tauri wraps it as desktop and mobile shells — same React SPA, remote API, hash router — so Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, and Android stay packaging, not forks.

platformsOverview.title: Thin packaging around apps/web
platformsOverview.body: Desktop lives in apps/desktop; mobile in apps/mobile. Both Vite-build the web app with VITE_API_URL and VITE_ROUTER=hash. No product UI in the shells — features stay in apps/web so every platform ships the same screens.
points: apps/desktop → Windows, Linux, macOS installers from GitHub Actions
apps/mobile → iOS via Xcode locally; same remote-API model for Android
WKWebView / native WebView use Bearer sessionToken when cookies won't stick on HTTP
Rename productName and identifier in tauri.conf.json when you fork

platformsLinks.title: How each OS ships
platformsLinks.body: Desktop builds are CI-ready. Mobile follows the same shell pattern — open a page for the install story and the running app mock.

android.title: Same shell idea on Android

structureDomain.title: Registrar. CNAME. Render.
structureDomain.body: Point app.example.com at your Render service with a CNAME, verify the domain, get a TLS cert, then set APP_URL so cookies and magic links use your host.

overview.title: One origin for the product
overview.body: This template is API + SPA on one host. A custom domain replaces the *.onrender.com URL for browsers — cookies, CORS, and emailed links all follow APP_URL.
points: Set APP_URL to the custom host

renderAdd.title: Add the custom host
renderAdd.body: Service → Settings → Custom Domains → Add Custom Domain. Enter app.example.com (or your subdomain). Render then shows the DNS records to create.

renderDns.title: The CNAME Render expects
renderDns.body: Hostname is usually the subdomain label (app). Target is your service’s onrender.com host. Create that exact CNAME at the registrar — then Render can verify and issue TLS.

godaddy.title: Create the CNAME at the registrar
godaddy.body: DNS management → Add new record → CNAME. Name = app (or www). Value = the onrender.com host from Render. Same idea on Cloudflare, Namecheap, Route 53 — only the UI changes.

renderDone.title: Verified + Certificate Issued
renderDone.body: When DNS matches, Render marks the domain Verified and issues a certificate. Traffic can use https://app.example.com — the onrender subdomain can stay enabled as a backup.

env.title: APP_URL on Render
env.body: After the custom domain is Verified, set APP_URL (and CORS_ORIGIN if needed) in Environment → Edit so magic links and cookies use https://app.example.com.
points: redeploy / restart if links still use onrender
env.visualFootnote: APP_URL = your verified custom host (sync: false).

chat.title: Conversation, tools, reply
chat.body: The panel streams status and tool chips as their own rows — then the final answer. Same tools as MCP, scoped to the current tenant.

fab.title: Corner button that keeps working
fab.body: Minimize to a FAB. Activity shows as a pill. ⌘J records without opening the panel; when the reply lands, the compact chat reopens.

chat.title: A chat that gets things done
chat.body: Ask or command. The assistant runs domain tools, shows each action as a chip, then answers. Write tools refresh the app data when they succeed.
points: Tool chips are timeline rows — not buried in the reply

chips.title: Pending, done, error
chips.body: tool_start shows a spinning chip with the progress label. tool_done swaps in the summarize text and a check — or an error chip if the tool failed safely.

empty.title: Suggestions to start
empty.body: First open shows an intro for the current tenant and one-click suggestion prompts. Mic is ready when the composer is empty.
points: Mic when there is no text

expanded.title: Near-fullscreen focus
expanded.body: Maximize widens the panel with a dimmed backdrop. Esc or the restore control returns to compact — Esc again closes.

fab.title: Sparkles in the corner
fab.body: When the panel is closed, a round FAB stays bottom-right. Open it to chat; while work continues minimized, the icon spins and a pill shows status.

fabBusy.title: Still working while minimized
fabBusy.body: Minimize mid-run: the FAB shows a spinner and the current activity (Thinking… or the tool progress). When the turn finishes, the compact panel opens again so you see the reply.

fabRecording.title: ⌘J without opening the panel
fabRecording.body: Hold a voice note from anywhere: ⌘/Ctrl+J starts recording on the FAB (destructive red + stop). Enter or ⌘J again finishes; the clip is transcribed, then sent as a user message.
points: Panel opens when the reply arrives

audio.title: Record inside the composer
audio.body: With an empty composer, the mic button starts an in-panel recording bar. Cancel with × or stop to transcribe and send. Transcribing… disables the field until text is ready.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard without leaving the page
shortcuts.body: Voice and dismiss are global while the agent is available. Enter sends typed messages (Shift+Enter for a newline).
